name: The Conant household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: conant_reuben

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of March 1835 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1835-05-20, 50 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1835-03-31 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `letter_list_returns` as `1835-05-20`, which reaches 1835-05-20 — 42 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. A RETURN IS A DATE AND NOT A CITATION: `letter_list_returns` carries no source per return, so this leg cites none and the corpus that printed it is named in the person's own `sources`. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1835-05-20 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Conant, Rben' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: No reliable record in the reviewed repository corpus and targeted exact/variant-name web sweep could be tied to this postal person with sufficient date/place discriminators. This is a documented no-corroboration result, not evidence that the person did not exist.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'Reuben' is read as male because it stands in the yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
